subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Les Misérables and Social Reform
description: A 60-second lesson on Les Misérables and Social Reform.

hook.text: Victor Hugo wrote a fifteen-hundred-page novel arguing that poverty itself was a crime against humanity.

buildup.text: Les Misérables followed an ex-convict, a dying mother, and an orphan through the streets of Paris.

discovery.text: Hugo had spent years in political exile, using fiction to attack injustice he could not fight directly.

twist.text: The French government tried to suppress the book, but smuggled copies spread across Europe rapidly.

climax.text: The novel pressured lawmakers and became a rallying cry for social reform across the continent.

punchline.text: A novel fought for justice when its author could not.

quiz.question: Why did Victor Hugo write Les Misérables?
options: To attack poverty and injustice through fiction while in exile
To document his personal travel adventures
